n6b.vad-ar-ett-grafikkort.1: What is a GPU, and why does memory matter?
n6b.vad-ar-ett-grafikkort.2: Language models run on GPUs. A GPU has thousands of small calculators working at the same time, and its own fast memory. To follow the rest of the module, one image is enough: a kitchen with a great many cooks, but a rather narrow door to the pantry.
n6b.vad-ar-ett-grafikkort.3: The cooks are the compute. A modern datacenter card like the H100 does about 990 TFLOPS in bf16, that is roughly 500 trillion multiplications per second, because each multiplication is counted together with an addition (FMA).
n6b.vad-ar-ett-grafikkort.4: The pantry is the GPU memory (VRAM), for example 80 GB. The model's weights and the KV cache live there.
n6b.vad-ar-ett-grafikkort.5: The door is the memory bandwidth, about 3.35 TB per second. Every ingredient the cooks use has to be carried in through it.
n6b.vad-ar-ett-grafikkort.6: When the dense reference model generates a token, about 16 GB of weights must be read through the door, but with a single user the cooks do only a little work with them. Mostly they wait for memory. This is called memory-bound, and explains why batching and quantization help. A token is a piece of text, not necessarily a whole word.
n6b.kv-cache-i-klartext.2: Without a cache the model reruns the growing sequence for each new token. The KV cache saves earlier tokens’ keys and values, so only the new position’s representation needs to be computed through the layers. The new token must still read and compare against earlier positions.
n6b.kv-cache-i-klartext.3: What is storedFor every earlier token, its key (the label) and value (the content) from attention are saved in every layer. Hence the name: K and V.
n6b.kv-cache-i-klartext.4: How it is usedFor a new token, only its own key, value and query are computed. The query is compared with all stored keys, and the stored values are mixed. Reads and attention work therefore grow with the context.
n6b.kv-cache-i-klartext.5: ResultThe same mathematical logits as without a cache, apart from floating-point rounding. The bars count positions whose K/V are computed: with a cache, only the new one. They do not show all attention operations or total runtime.
n6b.kv-cache-i-klartext.6: The priceIn the reference model’s bf16 cache each token costs 128 KiB. A conversation of 8000 tokens uses about 1.05 GB for as long as it runs.
